headline: Comparative genomics traces gene-family evolution and selection across vertebrates
label: Comparative Genome Architecture Inference
summary: Expanded comparative sequence collections, from 1,961 vertebrates to 363 avian genomes, now allow selection and copy-number changes to be tested directly.
synthesis: The three studies share a comparative framework in which large sequence collections are used to infer the evolutionary history of gene families and genomic elements. The Wnt study analyzes 38,886 sequences from 1,961 vertebrates, quantifying copy-number variation, whole-genome duplication effects and dN/dS rates. The CYP4 study applies site, branch and branch-site codon models across four subfamilies in 363 avian genomes to link selection patterns to lineage-specific evolution. The Drosophila study addresses a different question: an improved TEChim analysis indicates that intronic transposons form alternative exons in brain splice isoforms, and it rebuts a prior report. The dominant thread is comparative inference of gene repertoire and selection across genomes. What is new here is the extension of this approach from gene-family and codon-level evolution to transposon contributions to transcript structure.
